p.src: Now, when Baoyu heard Lady Wang summon him, he hurried to the front, where he learned that she intended to take him to pay a visit to Lady Zhen. Baoyu was naturally delighted and hastened to change his clothes before accompanying Lady Wang there. The appearance and circumstances of the household proved little different from those of the Rong and Ning mansions, though in one or two respects it was even grander. Upon making careful inquiries, he found that there really was a Baoyu in the family. Lady Zhen kept them for a meal, and they did not return until the end of the day; only then was Baoyu convinced. After they returned home that evening, Lady Wang ordered a first-rate banquet to be prepared and a celebrated theatrical troupe engaged, and invited Lady Zhen and her daughter over. Two days later, the mother and daughter took their leave without ceremony and returned to their official post; nothing further need be said of them.

p.src: Confronted with this, Baoyu felt as though a basin of cold water had suddenly been poured over his heart. He stared at the bamboo and stood there dazed for some time. As Nanny Zhu had just come to dig bamboo shoots and trim the canes, he wandered out in a stupor. For a while his soul seemed to desert him and his mind knew nothing; he sank at random onto a garden rock and stared blankly, until tears began to fall without his noticing. He remained there for the span of five or six meals, turning over a thousand thoughts, yet wholly unable to decide what he could do. It happened that Xueyan, returning this way with some ginseng from Lady Wang’s rooms, turned her head and caught sight of someone seated on a rock beneath a peach tree, cheek propped in hand and lost in thought. It was none other than Baoyu. Xueyan wondered, “It is bitterly cold—what is he doing out here all alone? “In spring, everyone with some lingering ailment suffers a relapse. Can his foolish sickness have come upon him again?” Thinking this, she went over, crouched beside him, and asked with a smile, “What are you doing here?” Catching sight of Xueyan, Baoyu suddenly said, “Why have you come looking for me too? “Are you not a girl as well? “Since she is anxious to avoid suspicion and will not let any of you pay attention to me, why have you come to seek me out? If someone sees us, will it not provoke more gossip? “Hurry back to your rooms.” Hearing this, Xueyan assumed that Daiyu had upset him yet again and had no choice but to return to their rooms.

p.src: At this, Zijuan hurriedly put down her needlework and told Xueyan to listen carefully for any summons. “If they ask for me, say I’ll be back at once.” With that, she left the Naiad’s House and went straight in search of Baoyu. When she reached him, she said with a smile, “I only said those few words for everyone’s good, yet you took offense, ran out here into the wind, and started crying. You’ll make yourself ill and frighten me.” Baoyu hastily smiled. “Who took offense?” “What you said seemed reasonable to me. I thought that if you all felt that way, others must feel the same, and that little by little everyone would cease to care about me. That was why I felt sorry for myself.” Zijuan then sat down close beside him. Baoyu smiled. “A moment ago you moved away even while speaking face-to-face with me. Why have you come to sit so close now?” “Have you forgotten?” Zijuan replied. “A few days ago, while you and your cousin were talking, Aunt Zhao walked in. I have just heard that she is not at home, so I came to ask you about it. The other day, you and she had only mentioned ‘bird’s nest’ before stopping, and the matter was never raised again. I have been meaning to ask you about it.” “It was nothing important,” Baoyu said. “I merely thought that Cousin Bao is herself a guest here. Since Daiyu is taking bird’s nest, she must not interrupt the treatment; but if she kept asking Cousin Bao for it, she would be imposing too much on her. Though it was awkward to ask Mother, I hinted at it before Grandmother. I expect Grandmother has spoken to Cousin Feng about it. I began telling her about it, but never managed to finish. Now I hear that you are being given one liang of bird’s nest every day, so the matter is settled.” “So it was you who spoke about it,” Zijuan said. “Thank you for taking so much trouble on our behalf. We had been wondering why Grandmother had suddenly thought of ordering someone to send us one liang of bird’s nest every day. That explains it.” Baoyu smiled. “If she takes it every day without interruption, two or three years should make her well.” “She may grow accustomed to taking it here,” Zijuan said, “but when she goes home next year, where will there be spare money for such things?” Baoyu started in alarm and asked hastily, “Who? Whose home is she going to?” “Your cousin is going home to Suzhou,” Zijuan replied. Baoyu laughed. “You are talking nonsense again. Suzhou may be her ancestral home, but it was because her father and mother died and no one was there to care for her that she came here. Whom would she go back to next year? Obviously you are lying.” Zijuan gave a cold laugh. “You think far too little of other people. Do you imagine that only your Jia family is a great clan with many members, and that apart from your family everyone else has merely a father and mother, with not another soul in the whole clan? When our young lady came here, it was because Grandmother pitied her for being so young. Though she had uncles, they could not take the place of her own parents, so Grandmother brought her here to stay for a few years.

p.src: Presently Nanny Li arrived. After examining him for some time, she asked him several questions, but received no answer. She felt his pulse, then pinched him hard twice above the upper lip, leaving deep fingernail marks, yet he showed no sign of pain. Nanny Li merely cried, “This is terrible!” Then, with a wail, she threw her arms around him and burst into loud sobs. In her distress, Xiren hurriedly pulled at her and said, “Please look carefully, Nanny Li—is his condition truly so grave? Tell us first, so that we can report it to Grandmother and Madam Wang. Why are you the first to start crying?” Beating the bed and pounding the pillow, Nanny Li cried, “He is beyond saving! All the worry I have spent on him throughout my life has been for nothing!” Xiren and the others had asked her to come because she was old and experienced. Now, hearing her speak this way, they believed it to be true and all began to weep.

p.src: Qingwen then told Xiren everything that had just happened. On hearing this, Xiren hurried to the Xiaoxiang Lodge. She found Zijuan attending Daiyu as she took her medicine, but, heedless of all propriety, went straight up and demanded, “What did you say to our Baoyu just now? Go and see him! You can answer to the Old Lady yourself—I wash my hands of it!” With that, she sat down on a chair. Daiyu, suddenly seeing Xiren’s face full of anger and alarm, stained besides with tears, and her whole manner so altered, could not help becoming frightened herself and hurriedly asked what had happened. After steadying herself for a moment, Xiren sobbed, “I don’t know what words Madam Zijuan said to him, but that fool’s eyes are staring, his hands and feet have gone cold, and he cannot speak. He did not even feel it when Nanny Li pinched him—he is more than half dead already! Even Nanny Li says there is no hope, and she is wailing her heart out over there. I fear he may be dead by now!” When Daiyu heard this, she reflected that Nanny Li was an experienced old woman; if she said there was no hope, then surely there could be none. With a cry, she choked up all the medicine in her stomach. Racked through entrails and lungs, scorched in stomach and liver, she suffered several fits of agonized coughing. In moments her face was flushed, her hair dishevelled, her eyes swollen and her veins bulging, and she gasped so hard that she could not raise her head. Zijuan hurried forward to thump her back. After lying over her pillow and gasping for a long while, Daiyu pushed her away and said, “There is no need to thump me. The proper thing would be to fetch a rope and strangle me!” Zijuan wept. “I said nothing, really—only a few words in jest. He took them seriously.” “You know what he is like,” said Xiren. “That simpleton is always taking jokes in earnest.” Daiyu said, “Whatever you told him, go quickly and explain it. Perhaps he will come round.” At this, Zijuan hurriedly got down from the bed and went with Xiren to Happy Red Court.

p.src: By evening Baoyu was a little better, and only then did Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and the others return to their rooms. Even so, they sent people several times during the night to inquire after him. Nurse Li led Nanny Song and several other elderly women in keeping careful watch, while Zijuan, Xiren, Qingwen, and the others stayed with him day and night. Baoyu was lucid by then, but because he feared that Zijuan would go back, he sometimes pretended to be deranged. Once Xiren and the others had regained their peace of mind, they joked with Zijuan, “You caused all this trouble, so now you must cure him. Who ever saw such a fool as ours, who hears the wind and thinks it must be rain? What are we to do with him from now on?” For the present, we leave the matter there.

p.src: In recent days, when Lin Daiyu heard of Baoyu’s condition, her illness inevitably worsened, and she wept several times more. Now, seeing Zijuan return, she asked what had happened and learned that Baoyu was almost recovered; she therefore sent Hupo back to attend Grandmother Jia. Late that night, after the household had settled and Zijuan had undressed and lain down, she quietly smiled at Daiyu and said, “Baoyu’s heart is true enough. The mere news that we might leave brought him to such a state.” Daiyu made no reply. After a long pause, Zijuan said as if to herself, “It is better to remain where one is than to make a change. This household of ours may certainly be called a fine family. Everything else is easy enough to find, but nothing is more precious than growing up together from childhood and knowing each other’s temper and disposition through and through.” Daiyu spat in disgust. “Have these past few days not tired you out? Why do you not rest while you can instead of spouting such nonsense?” Zijuan smiled. “This is no idle nonsense. I truly have your best interests at heart, miss. I have worried about you for years. With neither parents nor brothers, who is there to cherish you and look after your needs? The important thing is to settle this great matter early, while the old lady is still clear-minded and strong. As the saying goes, ‘An old person’s vigor is like a spring chill or autumn heat—it cannot last.’ If anything should suddenly happen to the old lady, the matter might still be concluded eventually, but I fear the proper time would be lost and the outcome would no longer be to your heart’s desire. There may be plenty of princes and noble young masters, but which of them does not keep three wives and five concubines, favoring one woman today and another tomorrow? Even if a heavenly beauty came to them, after three or five nights they would cast her out of mind; some even turn against one another over a concubine or maid. A woman with a powerful family behind her fares somewhat better. But for someone in your position, miss, each day the old lady lives is another day of protection; once she is gone, you will simply be left at the mercy of anyone who chooses to bully you. That is why I say it is vital to make up your mind. You are an intelligent person, miss. Surely you know the saying: ‘Ten thousand taels of gold are easily won, but a single kindred heart is hard to find.’” When Daiyu heard this, she said, “Has this girl stopped being mad today? How did a few days away turn you into a different person? Tomorrow I shall certainly ask the old lady to take you back. I dare not keep you any longer.” Zijuan laughed. “I have said nothing but what is good for you, merely asking you to keep it in mind. I never told you to do anything wicked. Why send me back to the old lady and make me suffer? What good would that do?” With that, she went straight to sleep. Although Daiyu had answered as she did, Zijuan’s words could not help but grieve her. Once Zijuan was asleep, Daiyu wept without pause through the night and only dozed off briefly at dawn. The next day she forced herself to wash and dress and ate a little bird’s-nest congee. Grandmother Jia and the others then came in person to see her and gave her many more instructions.

Xifeng sighed. “Aunt, you know how contrary our lady can be. Let me work this out gradually.” When Grandmother Jia later came to see Xifeng, Xifeng told her, “Aunt Xue has a favor to ask of you, Old Ancestress, but she finds it difficult to broach.” Grandmother Jia quickly asked what it was, and Xifeng explained the proposed marriage. Lady Xing considered the matter: the Xue family was of good standing and now very wealthy; Xue Ke was handsome; and Grandmother Jia insisted on acting as matchmaker. Taking advantage of the opportunity, she agreed. Grandmother Jia was delighted and promptly sent for Aunt Xue. When the two women met, they naturally exchanged many modest courtesies. Lady Xing immediately sent someone to inform Xing Zhong and his wife. The couple had come precisely to depend upon Lady Xing, so how could they object? They lost no time in declaring the match splendid. Grandmother Jia laughed. “I do enjoy meddling in other people's affairs! Today I have brought off another match. I wonder how much matchmaker's reward I shall receive?” Aunt Xue laughed. “Naturally, you shall have one. p.src: Xue Ke and Xiuyan had once met briefly on the journey some time before, and it seemed that each was well pleased with the other. Xiuyan, however, inevitably became somewhat more constrained than before. She felt unable to sit chatting freely with Baochai and the other girls, and since Xiangyun loved to tease people, she grew more embarrassed still. Fortunately, she was educated and understood proper conduct. Though naturally endowed with a young woman's modesty, she was not one of those frivolous, affected girls who feigned shyness and manufactured embarrassment at every turn. Ever since Baochai first met her, she had seen that Xiuyan's family was poor; moreover, whereas other people's parents were generally elderly and respectable, Xiuyan's alone were hopelessly besotted with drink and treated their daughter with indifference. Lady Xing showed her no more than the affection required to save appearances and did not truly care for her. Xiuyan herself was refined and dignified, while Yingchun was a living corpse with breath in her body, unable even to look after herself properly, let alone attend to Xiuyan. If Xiuyan lacked any of the ordinary things a young lady needed, there was no one to see to it, and she would never ask anyone for help. Baochai therefore often showed her consideration and secretly supplied her needs, taking care that Lady Xing should not learn of it, for fear that she might become suspicious or provoke gossip. Now, quite beyond anyone's expectations, an extraordinary turn of fate had brought about this marriage. In her heart, Xiuyan had first approved of Baochai, and only afterward of Xue Ke. Xiuyan would still sometimes chat with Baochai, and Baochai continued to address her as a sister.

p.src: That day, Baochai was on her way to visit Daiyu when she happened to meet Xiuyan, who was going to see Daiyu as well. Baochai smilingly called her over, and the two walked together behind a stone wall. There Baochai asked with a smile, “It is still bitterly cold. Why have you changed entirely into lined clothes?” At the question, Xiuyan lowered her head and made no reply. Baochai knew at once that there must be some reason for it, and asked again with a smile, “I suppose you have not received this month’s allowance either. That girl Xifeng has grown terribly thoughtless.” “She does remember to pay me on time,” Xiuyan replied. “But Aunt Xing sent someone to tell me that I could not possibly need two taels a month and should save one tael to send to my parents. If I needed anything, she said, Second Sister had plenty of things, so I could make do by using some of hers. If they were here, once Baoqin had married into their family, we could discuss your marriage again. But while they are away, nothing can be done. And until his younger sister’s marriage has first been settled, he would never dare marry before her. It really is a difficult situation. Yet if it is delayed another two years, I fear all this suffering will make you ill. Let me discuss it further with Mother. If anyone mistreats you, try to bear it patiently, and whatever you do, do not torment yourself into an illness. You might as well give them that other tael tomorrow and be done with it; then everyone’s mind will be at rest. From now on, you need not waste your money buying them food. Let them make all the cutting remarks they please; if they become unbearable, simply walk away from them. If you ever lack anything, do not stand on bashful ceremony like a timid young girl; just come to me. It is not merely because we are to become relatives; we have been close ever since you first arrived. Even if you fear gossip, you need only send a young maid to tell me privately.” Xiuyan lowered her head and assented. Baochai then pointed to a green-jade pendant on Xiuyan’s skirt and asked, “Who gave you this?” “Third Sister gave it to me,” Xiuyan replied. Baochai nodded and smiled. “She saw that everyone had one except you and feared people might laugh at you, so she gave you one. That shows how intelligent and thoughtful she is.

p.src: But there is something else you should understand. Such ornaments are properly worn by young ladies of powerful and wealthy families. Look at me from head to foot: do you see any of these lavish, superfluous adornments? Seven or eight years ago, I too dressed that way. But times have changed, and wherever I could economize, I have done so of my own accord. When you eventually join our family, I expect you will find a whole chestful of such useless things. Our circumstances are no longer equal to theirs. We must make simplicity and propriety our rule in everything and not try to imitate them.” Xiuyan smiled. “Since you say so, Cousin, I shall take it off when I return.” Baochai hastily laughed. “You take people’s words far too literally. She gave it to you out of kindness. If you do not wear it, will she not become suspicious? I only happened to mention the matter. Go back now and have a maid bring me the pawn ticket. I will redeem the clothes quietly and have them secretly delivered to you this evening, so you will have something warm to wear morning and night. Baochai laughed. “Well, this is amusing—we have kept it all in the family! If the shopmen find out, they will say, ‘The bride has not yet arrived, but her clothes have come ahead of her!’” Hearing this, Xiuyan realized that the pawnshop belonged to Baochai’s family. She could not help blushing and smiling, and the two went their separate ways.

p.src: Baochai made her way to the Xiaoxiang Lodge. Her mother happened to have come to see Daiyu as well, and the two were chatting. Baochai smiled. “When did you get here, Mother? I had no idea.” Aunt Xue said, “My days have been so busy lately that I have not had a chance to come and see Baoyu or her. So today I came to see them both, and they are both better now.” Daiyu quickly invited Baochai to sit down, then said to her, “The affairs of this world are truly beyond imagining. Who would ever have thought that Aunt Xue and First Aunt would become relations by marriage?” Aunt Xue said, “My dear child, what would young girls like you know of such things? As the old saying goes, ‘A marriage made across a thousand miles is joined by a single thread.’ There is an Old Man under the Moon who governs marriage. He determines every match beforehand and secretly ties the two people’s feet together with a red thread. Though their families may be separated by seas and countries, or even be hereditary enemies, in the end some chance will still bring them together as husband and wife. Such matters always turn out contrary to expectation. Even if both the parents and the couple themselves are willing, or the two have spent every year together and everyone assumes the match is settled, they can never come together unless the Old Man under the Moon has bound them with his red thread. Take the marriages of you two sisters: even now, no one knows whether your future husbands are close at hand or far beyond the mountains and seas.” Baochai said, “Only you, Mother, would drag us into the conversation whenever you start talking.” As she spoke, she nestled into her mother’s arms and said with a laugh, “Let us go.” Daiyu laughed. “Just look at her! Grown as she is, when she is away from Aunt Xue she is the very model of composure, but the moment she sees her mother she turns into a spoiled child.” Aunt Xue stroked Baochai and sighed as she said to Daiyu, “This sister of yours is just like Xifeng before the Old Lady. Whenever there is serious business, I discuss it with her; and when there is nothing pressing, thankfully she cheers me up. When I see her like this, no sorrow of mine can fail to melt away.” Hearing this, Daiyu shed tears and sighed. “She chooses to behave like this here precisely to torment a motherless girl like me, deliberately flaunting it before my eyes.” Baochai laughed. “Mother, just listen to her nonsense! And she calls me spoiled.” Aunt Xue said, “You cannot blame her for feeling sad. Poor child, with neither father nor mother, she has no close kin of her own after all.” Then, caressing Daiyu, she smiled and said, “There, dear child, do not cry. You are upset because you see me doting on your sister, but you do not know that in my heart I care for you even more. Though your sister has lost her father, she still has me and her own brother, so in that respect she is better off than you. I often tell your sister how deeply I care for you; I simply cannot show it openly in front of everyone.

p.src: There are so many people here and so much gossip. Few speak kindly, while many speak ill. Instead of saying that you have no one to depend upon and therefore deserve the affection and concern of others, they would only say that, seeing how the Old Lady dotes on you, we too were currying favor by following the tide.” Daiyu smiled. “Since you say so, Aunt, tomorrow I shall acknowledge you as my mother. If you disdain me and refuse, then your affection for me must be mere pretense.” Aunt Xue said, “If you do not find me unworthy, I would be delighted to have you do so.” Baochai hurriedly said, “You cannot acknowledge her as your mother.” “Why not?” asked Daiyu. Baochai smiled and asked, “Let me ask you this: my elder brother has not yet had a marriage arranged, so why was Cousin Xing promised to my younger cousin instead? What do you suppose the reason was?” Daiyu said, “Perhaps because he was away from home, or because their birth signs and birthdays were incompatible, she was promised to your younger cousin first.” Baochai laughed. “Not so. My brother has already set his heart on someone; he is merely waiting until he comes home to make the betrothal official. There is no need for me to name her. I just said that you could not acknowledge Mother as your own—think carefully and you will understand.” As she spoke, she exchanged a wink with her mother and burst out laughing. When Daiyu understood, she too threw herself against Aunt Xue and said, “Aunt, I will not let you off unless you punish her!” Aunt Xue quickly put her arms around Daiyu and laughed. “Do not believe your sister. She is only teasing you.” Baochai laughed. “I mean it. Mother, tomorrow you should ask the Old Lady to give her to you as a daughter-in-law. Would she not be better than anyone you could find outside the family?” Daiyu leaned over to grab her and said with a laugh, “You are getting more outrageous by the moment!” Aunt Xue hurriedly intervened, laughing, and separated them with her hands before they finally stopped. Then she said to Baochai, “Even with Miss Xing, I feared that your brother would mistreat her, so I arranged her marriage to your younger cousin instead. As for this child, I would never consent to giving her to him. The other day the Old Lady wanted to match your younger sister with Baoyu, but unfortunately she was already promised elsewhere; otherwise it would have been an excellent marriage. When I settled Miss Xing’s marriage the other day, the Old Lady even joked, ‘I had meant to ask for one of her family, but before I could get her, she carried off one of ours instead.’ It was said in jest, but when one thinks it over, there is some sense in it. Baoqin may already be promised, and I may have no one else to offer, but surely that does not mean I need say nothing at all. I was thinking: the Old Lady dotes so deeply on your Cousin Baoyu, and he is such a fine-looking boy that if she sought a bride outside the family, no one would ever satisfy her. Why not simply betroth your Cousin Lin to him? Would that not make everything perfect all around?” At first Lin Daiyu merely stared in bewilderment, but when she finally realized that the talk had turned to her, she spat playfully at Baochai, blushed, caught hold of her, and laughed. “I will teach you a lesson! Why did you provoke Aunt Xue into spouting all this shameless old nonsense?”

p.src: When no one else remained in the room, Baochai finally asked Xiangyun where she had found it. Xiangyun laughed. “I saw Zhuan’er, your younger sister-in-law’s maid, secretly pass it to Ying’er. Ying’er slipped it casually between the pages of a book, assuming I had not seen. I waited until they had gone out, then took a secret look, but I could not make head or tail of it. I knew you were all here, so I brought it for everyone to identify.” Daiyu quickly asked, “Can it be that she too had pawned some clothes? But if she had pawned them, why did she give the ticket to you?” Questioned so directly, Baochai felt she could not conceal the truth from the two of them, and therefore told them everything that had just happened. Daiyu remarked, “When the rabbit dies, the fox grieves; creatures mourn those of their own kind,” and could not help sighing over it. Shi Xiangyun grew angry. “Just wait until I go and question Second Cousin! How about I give that whole pack of old women and maids a good scolding to avenge you?” With that, she made to leave. Baochai hurriedly caught hold of her and laughed. “You are flying into another of your mad fits! Sit down at once.” Daiyu laughed. “If you were a man, you could go out and fight to right an injustice. But what business have you playing Jing Ke or Nie Zheng? It is truly absurd.” Xiangyun said, “If you will not let me go and question her, then tomorrow we should bring her to live with us in the Garden. Would that not be better?” Baochai laughed. “We can discuss it tomorrow.” As she spoke, someone announced, “The Third and Fourth Young Ladies have arrived.” On hearing this, the three of them promptly fell silent and said no more about the matter.
